articles.headline: Fincantieri to invest $100 million in robotics, artificial intelligence at shipyards
articles.description: MARINETTE, Wis. — Fincantieri, one of the world’s largest shipbuilders, announced plans to invest nearly $100 million in robotics, artificial intelligence and advanced automation at its shipyards around the world, including its three facilities in Wisconsin. The Italian-based company announced Oct. 15 that it was expanding its BOOST² — The Shipyard of the Future program, an initiative launched three years ago to develop and introduce new technologies into shipbuilding operations. The investment is part of the company’s 2026-2030 industrial plan. More than 450 employees at 13 shipyards worldwide have participated in the program, including employees at Fincantieri Marinette Marine and the company’s Wisconsin System of Shipyards. Fincantieri operates three Wisconsin facilities: Marinette Marine in Marinette, Bay Shipbuilding in Sturgeon Bay and ACE Marine in Green Bay. Marinette Marine specializes in military shipbuilding, including vessels for the U.S. Navy. Bay Shipbuilding constructs, repairs and converts commercial vessels, including Great Lakes freighters. ACE Marine specializes in aluminum vessels for military and commercial applications. The modernization program focuses on integrating artificial intelligence with robotics to improve production efficiency, workplace safety and construction quality.
